draft.title: The origins of Hinduism
card: Hinduism grew over thousands of years in the Indian subcontinent. This is the region of South Asia that includes present-day India.
Unlike many religions, Hinduism has no single founder. No one person started it at a known moment.
Its practices and ideas developed gradually, as many communities, teachers and writers added to them over time.
Because of this, Hinduism includes a wide range of beliefs and practices, and it is often described as a family of traditions rather than one fixed system.
draft.remember: Hinduism developed slowly over a very long time, with no one founder.

a.q: Which statement best describes how Hinduism began?
opts: It developed gradually over thousands of years
It was started by one teacher at a known date
It was set up by a council to unify local beliefs
It began as a reform movement within another religion
a.why: Hinduism grew slowly as many communities and teachers added to it. It is wrong to say one teacher started it on a known date, because Hinduism has no single founder.
a.clue: Think about whether anyone is named as its founder.

b.q: A student says, 'Hinduism must have started when its founder first taught in India.' Why is this claim mistaken?
opts: Hinduism has no single founder and developed gradually
Hinduism was founded by a group of teachers in one year
Hinduism began outside the Indian subcontinent
Hinduism has existed for only a few hundred years
b.why: Hinduism grew over thousands of years in the Indian subcontinent, so no one founder began it. The idea of a group founding it in one year is also wrong, because its development was gradual and not a single event.
b.clue: Check the claim's assumption that there was a founder.

a.best: It developed gradually over thousands of years

b.best: Hinduism has no single founder and developed gradually
